observations.observation: The article is a full single-object edition of Moussaieff M163, including an introduction, transcription, translation, notes, bibliography, and photographic plates.

M163 is described as purchased by Shlomo Moussaieff after a Christie's auction in June 1997; earlier provenance is unknown. It measures 16.5 cm in diameter and 5.5 cm in depth, has two small missing fragments and a faded rim patch, and carries 30 lines in square Jewish Aramaic script spiralling clockwise from the centre.

The source presents M163 as an aggressive curse or subjugation text commissioned by Mihlad and Baran sons of Mirdukh against Isha son of Ifra-Hormiz; the final section invokes Jesus, his father, and holy spirits.

The companion article is titled 'Jesus in the Magic Bowls. Apropos Dan Levene's "... and by the name of Jesus ..."', authored by Shaul Shaked, and printed in Jewish Studies Quarterly 6 (1999), pp. 309-319.

Shaked discusses a distinct Mandaic Schoyen Collection bowl, MS 2054/124, as an aggressive text with a developed egg historiola, named antagonists, and a concluding Christian Trinitarian formula; translated excerpts identify the first-person beneficiary as Rastuia son of Qaqai.

policy: Only factual metadata and project-authored summaries are ingested. The modern transcriptions, translations, and photographic plates remain withheld and are not copied into the public corpus.
